thread.title: Nasdaq Leads Sell-Off As 4 Top Stocks Reverse Badly | Investor's Business Daily

author: DAVID SAITO-CHUNG
title: Nasdaq Leads Sell-Off As 4 Top Stocks Reverse Badly | Investor's Business Daily
text:
Stocks today saw a limited bounce in late-afternoon trading. A 5% slide in Apple ( AAPL ) shares hit all of the major indexes hard. The Nasdaq fell more than 2.1%. The composite index is poised to drop sharply for a third straight session.
X Apple, a big winner among megacap techs since its breakout on Jan. 6, 2017, is falling sharply as it tries to pick itself up and build a base . The stock is trying to find support near its critical long-term 200-day moving average.
Meanwhile, quick and deep drops by stocks breaking out in recent weeks suggest that some institutional investors are still anxious to sell — even after the stock market issued a follow-through on Wednesday.
While not every follow-through works out, IBD research has found that every key market bottom since 1900 featured a follow-through confirmation of a budding new uptrend in stocks.
The stock market seems to be taking into account the future impact of what higher interest rates will have on the economy. European stocks have been falling hard on concerns over whether Italy will revise its budget to meet eurozone standards on debt levels.
Leading Stocks Express Weakness Meanwhile, Green Dot ( GDOT ), Penumbra ( PEN ) and Leaderboard stock Twilio ( TWLO ) sold off sharply. They provide the latest examples of highly rated companies that ran into a brick wall of sellers after staging new breakouts . Planet Fitness ( PLNT ) also erased gains from a new high, although its pattern was a bit too short to be a proper base.
Planet Fitness, which on Wednesday last week bolted past a 55.45 buy point in a later-stage flat base , rallied all of two sessions and gained just 4% from the breakout price. The stock on Monday slid 7% and got as low as 49.74, triggering the 8%-loss-cutting sell rule . Shares bounced off the 50-day moving average.
The stock staged an initial breakout from a first-stage cup with handle in the week ended May 26, 2017, when the small-cap leisure services play ran past a 21.31 buy point. In other words, Planet Fitness had already rallied as much as 159% before creating its latest flat base in recent weeks.
At around 3 p.m. ET, the Dow Jones industrial average slipped 1.5%. It dropped as much as 2% before cutting some of its loss. Apple is a Dow Jones industrial component. The iPhone giant sold off on news that smartphone components supplier Lumentum ( LITE ) cut revenue guidance for the fiscal second quarter by 17%.
Lumentum cratered more than 31% lower, hitting levels last seen in February of 2017.
Less Worse Than The Nasdaq The S&P 500 did better, falling around 1.1% as defensive areas of the market, such as REITs and utilities, showed relative strength. They buffered big sell-offs in fiber optic telecom gear, chip equipment, electronic products, medical products, data storage and telecom infrastructure stocks.
The Russell 2000 more or less matched the S&P 500's decline. The Dow utility average rose 0.2%, even as California utilities PG&E ( PCG ) and Edison International ( EIX ) tanked badly. Liabilities for the two utilities may be rising following wildfires that hit hard the Northern California town of Paradise and communities in Southern California.
In Other Financial Markets Crude oil fell despite reports that Saudi Arabia plans a production cut. U.S. near-term oil futures lost 0.7% to $59.75 a barrel and are now down roughly 1% year to date.
Investors got back into long-dated U.S. Treasuries. The yield on the benchmark 10-year note edged down 1 basis point to 3.18%, a day after the yield plunged 5 basis points on Friday amid a broad sell-off in U.S. equities. The spread between 3-month and 10-year bonds remains relatively narrow at 84 basis points. The 30-year bond yield is at 3.38%.
